name: Word of Wisdom
originalWord: λόγος σοφίας (lógos sophías, Gr.); חָכְמָה (chokhmáh, Hebr.)
meaning: A supernatural word that reveals God's plan or solution
description: The gift of the word of wisdom describes a word or insight given by the Holy Spirit that reveals God's perspective, plan, or solution for a specific situation. The Greek “logos sophias” does not refer to general wisdom, but rather to a specific, situational utterance from God. In the Bible, this gift is demonstrated, for example, by Solomon (1 Kgs 3), by the apostles in difficult decisions (Acts 6; Acts 15), or by Jesus himself, who revealed divine wisdom in conflict situations. This gift brings clarity, guidance, and divine strategy into complex situations and serves to lead and edify the church.

questions.text: I have experienced God showing me surprisingly clear solutions.
Others often ask me for advice in difficult situations.
I feel inner clarity when facing complex decisions.
It gives me joy to help people make good decisions before God.
It is important to me to find divine strategies for stuck problems rather than human compromises.
Others say that my advice has helped them to clearly see God's will in crises.
I see that my advice has helped people in a lasting way.
I have experienced this person contributing helpful and well-thought-out solutions in difficult situations.
This person's contributions often help others to make good decisions.

name: Word of Knowledge
meaning: Supernatural knowledge or insight into the secrets of God
description: The word of knowledge describes an insight or information given by the Holy Spirit about a person, situation, or spiritual reality that was not obtained through natural means. The term “logos gnoseos” refers to a specific revelation of knowledge. In the Bible, this gift is demonstrated, for example, by Peter, who recognizes Ananias's deception (Acts 5), or by Jesus, who knows people's thoughts and life situations (John 4). This gift serves to bring truth to light, help people, and make God's work visible.

questions.text: While praying, God has given me a specific image or word for someone else's situation.
Have there been moments when you recognized things about a situation that you could not have known beforehand?
Have you experienced God giving you special insights into people or situations?
I have a desire for God to reveal "secrets" to me so that I can serve people more effectively.
I want to understand God's thoughts and truths more deeply.
Others experience new clarity on spiritual topics through my insights.
I feel urged to bring hidden things to light.
I have observed that this person recognizes connections that others do not notice at first.
This person's insights help others to better understand situations.

name: Faith
meaning: Special, miracle-working faith that moves mountains
description: The gift of faith is a special confidence, wrought by the Holy Spirit, that God will act in a particular situation. It goes beyond general saving faith and is a supernatural trust in God's power and promises. The Greek “pistis” here describes a strong, firm trust in God's action. In the Bible, this gift is demonstrated in people like Abraham (Rom 4) or in the apostles, who boldly expected God to move. This gift strengthens others in faith and opens the door for God's supernatural intervention.

questions.text: Have you experienced trusting God especially in seemingly impossible situations?
Have there been moments when your trust in God has encouraged others?
Have situations changed for the better because of your faith?
I trust that God can also do great and impossible things.
I feel motivated to trust God even when others doubt.
My trust in God often strengthens the faith of other people.
By holding onto God's promise, goals were achieved that the team/church had long since given up on.
I have experienced this person firmly trusting that God can act even in difficult situations.
This person's trust visibly encourages and strengthens other people.

name: Gifts of Healings
meaning: Ability to heal the sick through God's power
description: The “gifts of healings” describe various manifestations of divine healing through the Holy Spirit. The Greek “charismata iamaton” is in the plural, indicating that God grants different kinds of healings—physical, emotional, or spiritual. In the Bible, healings by Jesus and the apostles are frequently described (e.g., Acts 3; Mark 16). This gift demonstrates God's compassion for suffering people and serves as a sign of His kingdom as well as an encouragement to faith.

questions.text: Have you experienced someone receiving physical or emotional healing after your prayer?
Do you frequently have the impulse to pray for sick people?
Have you experienced God granting healing through prayer?
Are you inclined to pray for the sick and expect healing?
I firmly believe that Jesus still heals today just as He did in the time of the apostles.
People report that they have experienced comfort or healing through my prayer.
Others specifically ask me to pray for their health.
I have experienced this person praying for people who are sick or burdened.
People report that they have received help or comfort through this person's prayer.

name: Working of Miracles
meaning: Performing supernatural acts of power through God's strength
description: The “working of miracles” describes supernatural acts of power from God that go beyond natural possibilities. The expression “energēmata dynameōn” literally means “effectual workings of power.” In the Bible, this gift is demonstrated, for example, by Moses, Elijah, Jesus, and the apostles. Miracles can be deliverances, provisions, wonders of nature, or other extraordinary interventions by God, confirming God's power and the gospel.

questions.text: Have you experienced situations in which God has intervened in a supernatural way?
Have you experienced God doing extraordinary things through your prayer?
I expect supernatural acts of God in my surroundings.
I have the deep trust that God still performs visible signs of His power today to confirm His word.
I believe that God can still perform miracles today.

I have experienced this person praying for situations that are difficult to resolve humanly.
This person's faith encourages others to expect extraordinary intervention from God.

name: Prophecy
meaning: Speaking on behalf of God for edification, exhortation, and comfort
description: Prophecy is the Holy Spirit-inspired speaking on behalf of God for the edification, exhortation, and encouragement of the church (1 Cor 14:3). The term “propheteia” literally means “to speak for someone.” Prophecy can be both revelation and the application of God's Word to a concrete situation. In the Bible, we see prophetic speech in Old Testament prophets as well as in the New Testament, for example with Agabus (Acts 11). This gift strengthens faith, corrects errors, and directs the church's focus toward God's will.

name: Discerning of Spirits
meaning: Distinguishing between divine, demonic, and human spirits
description: The discerning of spirits is the ability to recognize spiritual influences and to distinguish whether they originate from God, the human spirit, or demonic powers. The term “diakrisis pneumaton” means “distinguishing or testing of spirits.” In the Bible, this gift is demonstrated, for example, by Peter (Acts 5) or Paul (Acts 16). It protects the church from deception and helps to clearly recognize God's work.

questions.text: I sense whether something comes from God, people, or other sources.

I carefully test spiritual impressions.
I have experienced how God has revealed deception to me.

name: Speaking in Tongues
meaning: Speaking in other languages or in the prayer language of the Spirit
description: The gift of speaking in tongues describes speaking in a language not learned by the speaker, inspired by the Holy Spirit. The Greek “gene glosson” means “various kinds of languages.” In the Bible, this gift first appears at Pentecost (Acts 2) and is explained especially in 1 Corinthians 12–14. It can serve both as a personal prayer language and as a public sign of God's work.

I have a desire to communicate with God in prayer beyond my understanding.
I am open to supernatural expressions in prayer.

name: Interpretation of Tongues
meaning: Interpreting and translating speaking in tongues for the edification of the church
description: The interpretation of tongues is the ability to understand a message in tongues and make it understandable to others. The Greek “hermeneia glosson” means “translation or interpretation of languages.” This gift ensures that speaking in tongues serves to edify the church by making its meaning clear (1 Cor 14).

This person was able to explain prayers in languages to me that I did not understand.

name: Service / Diakonia
meaning: Practical serving and helping in the church
description: The gift of service describes a special ability to help others practically and to recognize needs. The Greek “diakonia” means “service” or “practical help.” In the Bible, this gift is particularly evident in the ministry of the first deacons (Acts 6). People with this gift contribute significantly to the smooth functioning of the church and ensure that people receive concrete help.

name: Teaching
meaning: Instructing in the truth of God
description: The gift of teaching is the ability to explain God's Word clearly, understandably, and faithfully. The term “didaskalia” refers to both the content and the activity of teaching. In the Bible, this gift is particularly associated with leadership responsibilities (Eph 4:11). It helps the church to understand God's truth and grow in faith.

name: Exhortation
description: The gift of encouragement or exhortation (“paraklesis”) describes the ability to strengthen, comfort, and encourage people to faith through words. The word is related to the term “Paraclete,” which is used for the Holy Spirit as the Comforter. This gift helps people to overcome difficult times and continue in their faith.

name: Giving
description: The gift of giving describes a special willingness and joy to generously share material or financial resources. The Greek “metadidonai” means “to share” or “to pass on.” In the Bible, we see examples of this in the early church (Acts 4). This gift makes God's provision visible and supports the work of the Kingdom of God.

name: Leading
meaning: Leading and organizing the church (like a helmsman)
description: The gift of leadership describes the ability to lead people, cast vision, and organize structures. The Greek word “proistamenos” means “to stand before” or “to lead.” In the Bible, this gift is associated with responsibility for the church (1 Thess 5). It helps coordinate ministries and ensures that the church moves forward together.

name: Mercy
meaning: Compassion and practical help for those who suffer
description: The gift of mercy describes a special compassion for people in need and the willingness to help them practically. The Greek “eleos” means “mercy” or “compassion.” In the Bible, mercy is described as an expression of God's character (Matt 5:7). People with this gift bring God's love especially to those who are suffering.

name: Apostleship
meaning: Being sent with authority to plant churches
description: The gift of apostleship describes a special calling to plant new works or churches and to initiate spiritual movements. The word “apostolos” means “messenger” or “one who is sent.” In the Bible, we see this gift in the apostles who spread the gospel and planted churches. This gift combines vision, leadership, and missionary dynamism.

name: Evangelist
description: The gift of the evangelist is the special ability to communicate the good news of Jesus to people in an understandable and persuasive way. The word “euangelistēs” means “proclaimer of the good news.” In the Bible, we see this gift, for example, in Philip (Acts 21). Evangelists help people to come to faith in Christ.

name: Pastor
meaning: Pastoring, shepherding, and caring for the church as a flock
description: The gift of the pastor describes the ability to spiritually accompany, protect, and nurture people. The Greek “poimēn” means “shepherd.” Jesus himself is described as the Good Shepherd (John 10). People with this gift care for the long-term spiritual growth and well-being of the church.
